final_vote_record.note: Second reading: vote 19038, 17-0-0. Vote 19042 (26.6.2013) is the first reading of a different bill (item 479138) and approved no law.

deviations: Knesset websites (fs.knesset.gov.il, www.knesset.gov.il) redirect to a geo-block maintenance page (HTTP 303) from this location, so gazette PDFs were read from the Internet Archive captures named in the sheet, voting and reading data from Open Knesset mirrors, and coalition composition from encyclopedia articles (English Wikipedia for the 27th, 30th, 31st, 32nd and 33rd governments; Hebrew Wikipedia for the 28th and 29th), as the sheet allows when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Beyond the mirror directories the sheet names, I used Open Knesset mirrors of other Knesset tables as Knesset records: plenum/kns_plenumsession and plenum/kns_plmsessionitem (agenda items with bill status per sitting, used for first-reading and final-reading dates), knesset/kns_status (status codes 111 = first reading, 114/117 = second/third reading, 141 = tabled for first reading), plenum/kns_documentplenumsession (to locate plenum records) and bills/kns_documentbill (to locate bill files).

Tallies not found for seqs 54, 61, 64, 67, 70, 73 and 79: the Knesset plenum records for those dates (14_ptm_532506.docx, 15_ptm_532925, 532896, 532894, 533057, 533062 .docx, 16_ptm_129201.doc) are not archived on the Internet Archive (404) and the Knesset site is geo-blocked; the NYU archive has no Knesset record for those dates (it held only 25.3.1998, used for seq 57).

Explanatory notes not consulted for any row: first-reading bill PDFs tried for seqs 54, 64 and 85 are not archived (404), the seq 73 bill could not be retrieved, and the rest were not attempted. The gazette for Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 34) (15_lsr_300419) could not be retrieved either.
The Internet Archive refused connections intermittently (rate limiting); fetches were retried with pauses.

Web search budget ran out after four searches (a limit shared across agents), so no press searches for pre-2003 tallies were possible. One results list (for the seq 85 query) included a link to a court judgment and an opinion column mentioning litigation over the 2009 budget law; I did not open them and used nothing from them, and I disregarded the search tool's summary text about that litigation. Another results list concerned a later (2018) Jerusalem amendment and was not used. A Jerusalem Post page of 7.4.2009 that I opened had no vote data and was not used.

Seq 85: the third-reading vote is not in the Knesset plenum-vote table (it holds two second-reading votes and seven reservation votes on the item), so the final tally comes from dated press (JTA, 7.4.2009), which names no voters.
Seq 57: Knesset session table dates the second/third-reading sitting (sessions 195/196) to 24.3.1998; the plenum record itself (session 196) and the gazette footnote say 25.3.1998, which I used.

Seq 82: plenum vote 6417 (17.7.2006) carries this Basic Law bill's title but the ItemID of the Knesset Law (Amendment No. 22) item; the Basic Law's first-reading date is taken from the agenda record (item 145304, status 111, 17.7.2006).

Seqs 73 and 79: whether one vote approved two laws (Amendment No. 6 to the President law with Knesset Amendment No. 34 in 2001; President Amendments No. 6 and No. 7 in 2003) is not established; agenda records list separate items, but the vote records were not found.

Hebrew Wikisource raw pages for Basic Law: The President and Basic Law: The Knesset were used for amendment lists and the consolidated text; a Knesset consolidated text of Basic Law: Jerusalem (main.knesset.gov.il yesod2.pdf, via the Internet Archive) was opened but not relied on.
No scratch subfolder was created, because the dispatch forbade writing files; all documents were streamed into memory and nothing was saved. No page about a court case was opened.
